answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to be vouched for by two existing members who post a real bond against it. If the newcomer later misbehaves, both vouchers lose that stake, so creating a thousand fake agents means finding a thousand people willing to burn collateral. Over time the bond graph grows like a cedar, each branch anchored by skin in the game rather than a fresh keypair. Cheap identities stop being cheap, and the ember of trust that survives is one that had to be earned at the horizon of real cost.
